;Arts and culture
*The 50th anniversary of the death of Father [[Vincent R. Capodanno]], the decorated [[United States Navy|Navy]] [[United States Navy Chaplain Corps|chaplain]], is commemorated with a Mass and documentary premiere. He was killed in 1967 along with ambushed [[United States Marine Corps|Marines]] during the [[Vietnam War]]. ;Business and economy
*[[List of airlines of Germany|Airlines of Germany]]
**[[Air Berlin]], Germany's second largest airline, files for bankruptcy protection after its main shareholder, [[Abu Dhabi]]-based [[Etihad Airways]], chose not to make more financing available. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-40935559 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Disasters in [[Portugal]]
**A tree falls over at a religious ceremony in [[Funchal]], [[Madeira]], killing at least 12 people and injuring over 50 others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-40940007 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Libyan Civil War]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] issues an arrest warrant against [[Mahmoud al-Werfalli]] for the [[war crime]] of murder following the circulation of several videos in which he appears to oversee the execution of over 30 prisoners. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-warcrimes-libya-idUSKCN1AV1NU (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*Aftermath of the [[Unite the Right rally]]
**During a press conference at [[Trump Tower]] in New York City, which was intended to announce an [[executive order]] on [[infrastructure]] policy, President [[Donald Trump]] defended his August 12 remarks about the Charlottesville rally, placing "blame on both sides" for the incidents at the rally and criticizing what he referred to as the "alt-left," equating them with white supremacists and neo-Nazis on the right. [http://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-lashes-alt-left-charlottesville-fine-people-sides/story?id=49235032 (ABC News)] [http://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-defends-all-sides-comment-n793001 (NBC News)]
**[[Alliance for American Manufacturing]] president Scott Paul, [[AFL–CIO]] president [[Richard Trumka]] and the union's former chief of staff Thea Lee resign from President Trump's [[American Manufacturing Council]] due to their disagreements with Trump's response to the rally. The three corporate executives join [[Merck & Co.|Merck]] CEO [[Kenneth Frazier]], [[Intel]] CEO [[Brian Krzanich]] and [[Under Armour]] CEO [[Kevin Plank]], who also resigned from the council in protest the day prior. [https://www.cnbc.com/2017/08/14/intel-ceo-quit-trumps-manufacturing-council.html (CNBC)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/15/business/trump-councils-ceos.html (''The New York Times'')]
